# origincloud_dns_record_sets (Data Source)

Lists a zone's record sets by `dns_name`, then by `type`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "origincloud_dns_record_sets" "example" {
  project     = "my-project-123"
  hosted_zone = "hz-XEkE66gA3ma"
}

# The zone's names and types.
output "records" {
  value = [for r in data.origincloud_dns_record_sets.example.record_sets : "${r.dns_name} ${r.type}"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hosted_zone` (String) The hosted zone whose record sets to list.
- `project` (String) The project whose record sets to list.

### Read-Only

- `record_sets` (Attributes List) The record sets listed, from every page. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--record_sets))

<a id="nestedatt--record_sets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `record_sets`

Read-Only:

- `alias` (Attributes) The address of a platform resource, followed as it changes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--record_sets--alias))
- `basic` (Attributes) Values of its own. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--record_sets--basic))
- `create_time` (String) When the record set was created. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `dns_name` (String) The name the records answer for: the zone's `dns_name` or a name below it, written in full, such as `www.example.com`, without the final dot; answered in lowercase. Labels may hold `_` (`_dmarc.example.com`), and `*` only as the whole leftmost label, for a wildcard.
- `name` (String) The record set's resource name.
- `ttl` (String) How long resolvers may keep the answer, from 30 seconds to 7 days, in whole seconds. 300 seconds when left out. A duration in seconds, such as `90s` or `1.5s`.
- `type` (String) The records' type. An alias is `A`. One of `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `TXT`, `MX`, `SRV`, `CAA`.
- `update_time` (String) When the record set was last changed. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `urn` (String) The record set's URN, the identifier access policies and the audit log use.

<a id="nestedatt--record_sets--alias"></a>
### Nested Schema for `record_sets.alias`

Read-Only:

- `floating_ip` (String) The Floating IP whose address the record set answers with, in the zone's project. A Floating IP's address is an IPv4 address, so the record set is of type `A`; an `AAAA` alias is refused.


<a id="nestedatt--record_sets--basic"></a>
### Nested Schema for `record_sets.basic`

Read-Only:

- `values` (Set of String) The records' values, 1 to 100, each once, written as `type` says. Names are written in full without the final dot, and answered in lowercase. - `A`: an IPv4 address, `192.0.2.10`. - `AAAA`: an IPv6 address, `2001:db8::10`. - `CNAME`: one name, `www.example.net`. - `TXT`: the text as it is, printable ASCII, up to 4000 characters, without quotes; it is split into strings of 255 characters on the wire. - `MX`: `{preference} {exchange}`, `10 mail.example.com`. `0 .`, alone, says the name takes no mail. - `SRV`: `{priority} {weight} {port} {target}`, `10 5 5060 sip.example.com`. A target of `.`, alone, says the service isn't offered. - `CAA`: `{flags} {tag} {value}`, `0 issue letsencrypt.org`: flags 0 or 128, the value as it is, without quotes.

A record set's records take at most 16 KiB on the wire.
